reviews.frank_statement: Model output is proposal/EffectIntent and is not execution authority; EffectPermit remains opaque and host-minted.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A sufficiently typed model-visible authority token could safely authorize external effects without a distinct host capability domain.
reviews.falsifier: Demonstrate an end-to-end model-visible authority representation that remains non-forgeable, non-amplifiable, revocable and prompt-injection safe across serialization/FFI/process boundaries without an external authority root.
independent_checks: WASI.dev capability sandbox: components begin with no ambient authority and act only through host-granted capabilities.
Wasmtime security model: all outside interaction is through explicitly linked imports/exports; WASI filesystem access is capability based.
SEAgent arXiv:2601.11893 independently frames agent-tool over-privilege/confused-deputy failures and enforces mandatory access control outside the LLM.
adversarial_checks: EXP-CC-RC1.9-CBEL-TV-E2B-001: forged/invalid authority dimensions were rejected by the full gate; removing signature or scope admitted all targeted invalid cases.
Lane C authority/origin tests: model/current-producer identity alone was insufficient and origin-bound host policy prevented constructed laundering.
reviews.reason: The exact ClayCode encoding remains experimental, but the authority-separation class is independently supported and survived direct adversarial mechanism tests.

reviews.frank_statement: Effect commit revalidates current intent, basis/source state, selection, revocation, closure, recovery/resource conditions rather than trusting an earlier admission decision.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Some of basis, selection, closure, revocation or expiry are operational metadata and may be dropped during lowering without changing admissible effect behavior.
reviews.falsifier: Across adversarial stale/reselection/revocation/closure corpora and at least two representation boundaries, remove each candidate field independently and observe no new false authorization relative to an independently specified effect oracle.
independent_checks: Wasmtime/WASI capability practice independently supports explicit current host-granted scope rather than ambient authority.
Axon verified-compiler work (arXiv:2605.01660) independently supports translation validation/credible compilation as a way to check semantics across lowering boundaries.
WebAssembly Component Model Canonical ABI independently demonstrates stable typed interface meaning across different host-language layouts.
adversarial_checks: Local differential test: 100000 mixed cases, 0 reference/lowered authorization mismatches; each dropped field produced 5000/5000 targeted false accepts.
E2B EXP-CC-RC1.9-CBEL-TV-E2B-001: 30000 mixed cases, 0 mismatches/false accepts; each of eight dropped checks produced 2500/2500 targeted false accepts.
E2B EXP-CC-LANE-B-CROSSBOUNDARY-002: C FFI and JSON subprocess, 12000 cases each, 0 mismatches; each dropped check produced 1000/1000 targeted false accepts.
reviews.reason: The tested bound tuple is causally relevant in constructed differential experiments and the preservation method has independent compiler/capability precedent. Production FRANK and real capability-object/WASI red-team evidence are still absent, so the exact tuple remains an open candidate rather than a proven universal minimum.

reviews.frank_statement: Semantic identity is distinct from physical placement/wire/ABI representation, but correctness and authority obligations survive lowering.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A single representation identity is sufficient; ABI/process/backend changes need no explicit semantic translation witness if types compile.
reviews.falsifier: Show that independently implemented lowerings across materially different ABIs/processes preserve all declared semantic/effect outcomes without translation receipts and without representation-sensitive failures.
independent_checks: WebAssembly Component Model Canonical ABI explicitly separates language-internal layouts from the canonical cross-component ABI.

Axon credible compilation and other verified-compilation work provide independent precedent for checking semantic preservation across compiler stages rather than equating successful code generation with correctness.
adversarial_checks: E2B cross-boundary C-FFI and JSON-process differential execution compared each representation to the same reference decision semantics and found 0 mismatches in 12000 cases per boundary.
Single-check C mutants demonstrate that a compiling ABI adapter can still be semantically unsafe if it drops authority-relevant meaning.
reviews.reason: Independent ABI/compiler evidence and the current differential experiments support separating semantic identity from physical representation while requiring semantic-preservation checks.

reviews.frank_statement: UNKNOWN causal/dependency closure must not silently cast to valid for consequential effects.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Unknown closure can be treated optimistically as valid when a capability and intent otherwise match, because authorization scope already bounds harm.
reviews.falsifier: Under stale/hidden-dependency and prompt-injection corpora, optimistic UNKNOWN admission causes no additional consequential false accepts or safety regressions at matched utility/cost.
independent_checks: Memory-poisoning literature (arXiv:2606.04329) independently shows that untrusted contextual state can persist into later agent behavior, motivating use-time contextual validation rather than origin-only acceptance.
SEAgent confused-deputy analysis independently supports context-sensitive least-privilege checks at tool-use time.
adversarial_checks: E2B closure mutant: removing the closure check admitted 2500/2500 targeted UNKNOWN/invalid cases in experiment 001 and 1000/1000 across the C-FFI mutant in experiment 002.
reviews.reason: Fail-open UNKNOWN is directly unsafe in the constructed effect oracle and context-sensitive agent security supports revalidation, but the exact broaden/recompute/deny policy must still be tuned on live utility/risk traces.

reviews.frank_statement: FRANK untrusted cognition must not directly construct irreversible protected-state authority/effects.
reviews.counterhypothesis: The safest general language should make destructive/admin/raw effects entirely inexpressible at the source-language level.
reviews.falsifier: A general-purpose coverage suite shows that removing destructive/admin/raw effect requests does not reduce the ability to implement legitimate administrator, storage-engine, formatter, kernel/driver or embedded workloads, while preserving equivalent security through language restriction alone.
independent_checks: WASI capability design independently separates what an application can describe/compute from what the host grants it authority to access.
Wasmtime sandboxing independently enforces outside interaction through explicit interfaces rather than relying on source-language word bans.
adversarial_checks: Lane A general-purpose proxy covered 11/11 application classes only by retaining typed destructive/raw effect requests behind capabilities.
CC13 and Lane C counterexamples show constructive-only behavior can still be harmful, so destructive inexpressibility alone is not a sufficient safety boundary.
reviews.reason: The FRANK deployment safety requirement is retained, but the language-level interpretation is narrowed: destructive/admin/raw operations remain expressible as typed non-authoritative EffectIntent values; the untrusted FRANK profile lacks ambient matching authority and cannot mint EffectPermit.
